title: Ledger assembler for per-route / model / customer cost & latency decomposition
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a robust backend service (ledger assembler) that ingests token-level telemetry and routing metadata and emits daily and realtime decomposed metrics for cost and latency by route, model variant, and customer (tenant).

Scope:
- Ingest sources from request-trace stream (kafka) + model runtime metrics (prom/push gateway) + billing price catalog.
- Join and attribute per-token compute, queue, and memory overhead into unified decomposition vectors per request.
- Produce two outputs: near-realtime per-route streaming deltas for the Console and hourly/daily rollups for billing pipelines.
- Support multi-model request fanout (requests that hit ensembles or model fallback chains) and partial attribution across variants.

Non-goals: full chargeback billing runs (this service emits inputs consumed by billing), complex multi-customer pooling rules (later).

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end pipeline that computes per-request decomposition and materializes per-route/model/customer aggregates with <5% variance vs ground-truth offline baseline on synthetic workload.
- Streaming latency under 30s for 95th percentile of updates to Console when running at 2x current peak QPS.
- Rollout can be toggled per-namespace and includes a safe-fallback to the existing simple cost estimator.

Architecture notes:
- Use a lightweight stateless assembler service that consumes enriched events from kafka topics (trace.enriched, runtime.metrics), writes intermediate joins to RocksDB-backed state for windowed aggregation, and emits aggregate messages to out topics (console.metrics.delta, billing.rollup).
- Use a deterministic attribution algorithm (priority: model compute time, then queue time, then I/O) with configurable weights per product route to support business overrides.
- Persist daily ledgers to S3 as compressed parquet and register manifests for the billing consumer.

Performance targets and sizing:
- Designed to handle 30k RPS of request traces with average sequence lengths of 512 and 95th token fanout 1.3.
- Memory bound window size for hourly joins under 64GB per replica; horizontal scale by partition.

Security & compliance:
- All telemetry that contains customer identifiers must be hashed at ingest; raw PII never persisted beyond transient state stores.
- KMS-encrypt S3 ledgers and enable audit logging for ledgers access.

Testing and validation:
- Synthetic replay harness that replays production trace samples and compares decompositions against baseline offline batch job.
- Canary toggles and shadow-mode run for 48h before defaulting to traffic.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy assembler in shadow mode for low-traffic namespaces (2 days).
2) Run A/B of console display with old estimator vs new assembler for selected customers (1 week).
3) Gradually expand to 50% tenants and then full coverage with monitoring alarms for drift and cost anomalies.

2025-02-18 Marco Ruiz: Spike completed to validate RocksDB-backed windowed joins. Observed acceptable tail latencies with 2 partitions per vCPU. Added memory limit caveat to description.
2025-02-24 Design review (Jin Seo): Console UX team requested an additional 'attribution confidence' score to show when attribution is approximate due to fallback chains.
2025-03-01 Eng sync: Decided on deterministic weighting config stored in Config Service. Added runbook steps for switching to fallback estimator. Created feature flag 'ledger.assembler.active'.

2025-03-04 Marco Ruiz: Implemented prototype connector to billing.rollup topic and validated parquet manifest output to S3 in staging. Observed 3% deviation vs offline baseline on sample dataset. Moving to shadow canary next.
2025-03-04 QA (Elena Gomez): Added tests for multi-model fanout attribution and for hashed customer IDs to ensure no raw PII persists.
